title: The eight curve assertions pass to retracts
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-algebraic-closure], let $X$ be a separated scheme of finite type over $k$ with $\dim X\le1$, and let $G$, $H$ be torsion abelian sheaves on $X_{\Et}$, so that $(X,G)$ and $(X,H)$ are curve coefficient pairs [def-weil-pbc-curve-setting]. Let $a:G\to H$ and $b:H\to G$ be morphisms of abelian sheaves with $b\circ a$ an automorphism of $G$. Assume that $H$ is constructible whenever $G$ is [def-weil-pbc-constructible-torsion], that $H$ is torsion prime to $\operatorname{char}k$ whenever $G$ is, and that $H$ is $p$-primary whenever $\operatorname{char}k=p>0$ and $G$ is $p$-primary [def-weil-pbc-primary-torsion]. If the eight assertions $\mathcal C(X,H)$ of [def-weil-pbc-eight-curve-assertions] hold, then $\mathcal C(X,G)$ hold.

source.place: Etale Cohomology, Section 03SB, proof of Lemma 03SD (lemma-vanishing-easier), first paragraph: 'maps G -> f_*f^{-1}G -> G whose composition is an isomorphism. Hence it suffices to prove the lemma with F = j_!f_*f^{-1}G' (the passage to the summand, left implicit in Stacks)

proof.text: *Retraction.* Let $c=b\circ a$, an automorphism of $G$, and put $r=c^{-1}\circ b:H\to G$. Then $r\circ a=c^{-1}\circ(b\circ a)=c^{-1}\circ c=\mathrm{id}_G$, so $G$ is a retract of $H$ with section $a$ and retraction $r$. (Equivalently $e=a\circ r$ is an idempotent endomorphism of $H$ and $(r,\mathrm{id}-e):H\xrightarrow{\sim}G\oplus\ker r$, $a$ identifying $G$ with $a(G)=\operatorname{im}e$; only the identity $r\circ a=\mathrm{id}_G$ is used below.)

source.place: Etale Cohomology, proof of Lemma 03SD (lemma-vanishing-easier), first paragraph: 'maps G -> f_*f^{-1}G -> G whose composition is an isomorphism. Hence it suffices to prove the lemma with F = j_!f_*f^{-1}G' (the passage to the summand, left implicit there and written out here)

proof.text: *Cohomology and inverse images carry the retraction.* For a scheme $T$ and morphisms $\varphi:F\to F'$, $\varphi':F'\to F''$ of abelian sheaves on $T_{\Et}$, the maps $H^q(\varphi)$ of [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-functorial] (computed on fixed K-injective resolutions $s:F\to I^\bullet$, $s':F'\to I'^\bullet$, $s'':F''\to I''^\bullet$ of [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology] by lifts $\tilde\varphi$ with $\tilde\varphi s\simeq s'\varphi$, independent of the lift) satisfy $H^q(\varphi'\circ\varphi)=H^q(\varphi')\circ H^q(\varphi)$ and $H^q(\mathrm{id}_F)=\mathrm{id}$: $\tilde\varphi'\tilde\varphi s\simeq\tilde\varphi's'\varphi\simeq s''\varphi'\varphi$, so $\tilde\varphi'\circ\tilde\varphi$ is a lift of $\varphi'\varphi$, and $\mathrm{id}_{I^\bullet}$ is a lift of $\mathrm{id}_F$, and $\mathcal H^q(\Gamma(T,-))$ preserves composites and identities. So $H^q(T_{\Et},-)$ is a functor $\Ab(T_{\Et})\to\Ab$, and by [lem-weil-pbc-functor-preserves-retract] $H^q(X_{\Et},G)$ is a retract of $H^q(X_{\Et},H)$, with section $\alpha_q=H^q(a)$ and retraction $\beta_q=H^q(r)$, $\beta_q\alpha_q=\mathrm{id}$. Likewise, for a morphism of schemes $u:Y\to X$, the inverse image $u^{-1}$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] is a functor, so (same lemma) $u^{-1}G$ is a retract of $u^{-1}H$ with section $u^{-1}a$ and retraction $u^{-1}r$, and applying the functor $H^q(Y_{\Et},-)$ once more, $H^q(Y_{\Et},u^{-1}G)$ is a retract of $H^q(Y_{\Et},u^{-1}H)$ with section $\alpha'_q=H^q(u^{-1}a)$ and retraction $\beta'_q=H^q(u^{-1}r)$, $\beta'_q\alpha'_q=\mathrm{id}$.

source.place: Etale Cohomology, proof of Lemma 03SD (lemma-vanishing-easier), first paragraph: 'maps G -> f_*f^{-1}G -> G whose composition is an isomorphism. Hence it suffices to prove the lemma with F = j_!f_*f^{-1}G' (the passage to the summand, left implicit there and written out here)

proof.text: *The pullback maps form a retract of arrows.* Let $u:Y\to X$ be a morphism of schemes and $u^*_G:H^q(X_{\Et},G)\to H^q(Y_{\Et},u^{-1}G)$, $u^*_H$ the pullback maps of [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback] (independent of the resolutions, clause 1 of [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-functorial]). Clause 3 (naturality) of [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-functorial], applied to $\varphi=a$ and to $\varphi=r$, gives $u^*_H\circ\alpha_q=\alpha'_q\circ u^*_G$ and $u^*_G\circ\beta_q=\beta'_q\circ u^*_H$. Together with $\beta_q\alpha_q=\mathrm{id}$ and $\beta'_q\alpha'_q=\mathrm{id}$ (step 2), $u^*_G$ is a retract of $u^*_H$ in the category of arrows of $\Ab$.

source.place: Etale Cohomology, proof of Lemma 03SD (lemma-vanishing-easier), first paragraph: 'maps G -> f_*f^{-1}G -> G whose composition is an isomorphism. Hence it suffices to prove the lemma with F = j_!f_*f^{-1}G' (the passage to the summand, left implicit there and written out here)

proof.text: *Vanishing: $\mathcal C_1$, $\mathcal C_2$, $\mathcal C_3$.* Let $q$ be in the range of one of these assertions for $(X,G)$: $q>2$ for [def-weil-pbc-C1]; $q>1$ with $X$ affine for [def-weil-pbc-C2]; $q>1$ with $\operatorname{char}k=p>0$ and $G$ $p$-primary for [def-weil-pbc-C3], in which case $H$ is $p$-primary by hypothesis [def-weil-pbc-primary-torsion]. In each case the hypotheses of the same assertion for $(X,H)$ hold (the condition on $X$ is the same; the torsion condition passes to $H$), so $H^q(X_{\Et},H)=0$. By step 2, $H^q(X_{\Et},G)$ is a retract of the zero object $H^q(X_{\Et},H)$ of the abelian category $\Ab$, hence is zero by [lem-weil-pbc-retract-of-zero-object].

source.place: Etale Cohomology, proof of Lemma 03SD (lemma-vanishing-easier), first paragraph: 'maps G -> f_*f^{-1}G -> G whose composition is an isomorphism. Hence it suffices to prove the lemma with F = j_!f_*f^{-1}G' (the passage to the summand, left implicit there and written out here)

proof.text: *Finiteness: $\mathcal C_4$, $\mathcal C_5$.* If $G$ is constructible [def-weil-pbc-constructible-torsion] and prime to $\operatorname{char}k$ [def-weil-pbc-primary-torsion] (for [def-weil-pbc-C4]), resp. $X$ is proper over $k$ and $G$ is constructible (for [def-weil-pbc-C5]), then by hypothesis $H$ is constructible, resp. constructible and prime to $\operatorname{char}k$, so the same assertion for $(X,H)$ says that $H^q(X_{\Et},H)$ is finite for every $q\ge0$. Since $\beta_q\circ\alpha_q=\mathrm{id}$ (step 2), $\alpha_q:H^q(X_{\Et},G)\to H^q(X_{\Et},H)$ is injective, so $H^q(X_{\Et},G)$ is isomorphic to the subgroup $\alpha_q(H^q(X_{\Et},G))$ of a finite group and is finite.

source.place: Etale Cohomology, proof of Lemma 03SD (lemma-vanishing-easier), first paragraph: 'maps G -> f_*f^{-1}G -> G whose composition is an isomorphism. Hence it suffices to prove the lemma with F = j_!f_*f^{-1}G' (the passage to the summand, left implicit there and written out here)

proof.text: *Isomorphism: $\mathcal C_6$, $\mathcal C_7$.* Let $k'/k$ be an algebraically closed extension, $\pi:X_{k'}\to X$ the projection, and assume $G$ prime to $\operatorname{char}k$ (for [def-weil-pbc-C6]; then $H$ is prime to $\operatorname{char}k$ by hypothesis) or $X$ proper over $k$ (for [def-weil-pbc-C7]). The map $\rho^q_{k'/k}(X,F)$ of [def-weil-pbc-extension-pullback] is the pullback map $\pi^*_F$ of [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback] for $u=\pi$, $F=G,H$. By the same assertion for $(X,H)$, $\rho_H=\pi^*_H$ is an isomorphism. With $\alpha=\alpha_q,\beta=\beta_q,\alpha'=\alpha'_q,\beta'=\beta'_q$ of step 2 for $u=\pi$ and $\rho_G=\pi^*_G$, step 3 gives $\rho_H\alpha=\alpha'\rho_G$ and $\rho_G\beta=\beta'\rho_H$. Put $\sigma=\beta\circ\rho_H^{-1}\circ\alpha'$. Then $\sigma\rho_G=\beta\rho_H^{-1}\alpha'\rho_G=\beta\rho_H^{-1}\rho_H\alpha=\beta\alpha=\mathrm{id}$ and $\rho_G\sigma=\rho_G\beta\rho_H^{-1}\alpha'=\beta'\rho_H\rho_H^{-1}\alpha'=\beta'\alpha'=\mathrm{id}$, so $\rho_G=\rho^q_{k'/k}(X,G)$ is an isomorphism, for every $q\ge0$. (A retract of an isomorphism is an isomorphism; Mathlib: MorphismProperty.IsStableUnderRetracts.isomorphisms.)

source.place: Etale Cohomology, proof of Lemma 03SD (lemma-vanishing-easier), first paragraph: 'maps G -> f_*f^{-1}G -> G whose composition is an isomorphism. Hence it suffices to prove the lemma with F = j_!f_*f^{-1}G' (the passage to the summand, left implicit there and written out here)

proof.text: *Surjectivity: $\mathcal C_8$.* Let $w:W\hookrightarrow X$ be an open immersion; the restriction map $w^*:H^2(X_{\Et},F)\to H^2(W_{\Et},w^{-1}F)$ of [def-weil-pbc-C8] is the pullback map of [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback] for $u=w$ (clause 5 of [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-functorial] identifies it with $\mathcal H^2$ of the restriction of an injective resolution). By $\mathcal C_8(X,H)$, $w^*_H$ is surjective (no hypothesis on the sheaf). Let $y\in H^2(W_{\Et},w^{-1}G)$; then $\alpha'_2(y)=w^*_H(x)$ for some $x\in H^2(X_{\Et},H)$, and by step 3 $w^*_G(\beta_2(x))=\beta'_2(w^*_H(x))=\beta'_2\alpha'_2(y)=y$. So $w^*_G$ is surjective. (A retract of an epimorphism is one; Mathlib: MorphismProperty.IsStableUnderRetracts.epimorphisms.)

source.place: Etale Cohomology, proof of Lemma 03SD (lemma-vanishing-easier), first paragraph: 'maps G -> f_*f^{-1}G -> G whose composition is an isomorphism. Hence it suffices to prove the lemma with F = j_!f_*f^{-1}G' (the passage to the summand, left implicit there and written out here)

proof.text: *Conclusion.* Steps 4 to 7 give each of the eight assertions for $(X,G)$ whenever its hypotheses are met, i.e. $\mathcal C(X,G)$ [def-weil-pbc-eight-curve-assertions].
